deep.reconstruction:
Caveat: the page is extremely faint. The ink has largely faded or bled through, and almost no formula can be read with confidence. What follows is a tentative reconstruction, guided by the clearly legible context of folios 1v and 2v. Everything beyond the visible fragments is my inference and is marked as such.

Context. The previous page sets up linearized perturbation equations for a homogeneous fluid ellipsoid in the style of Riemann's 1861 paper 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoides'. It has Euler-type equations dg/dt = rh - qk, etc., coupling the vorticity-like quantities (g,h,k) and the angular velocity (p,q,r). It linearizes about g = 0, p = 0 with exponent lambda and splits delta p = delta u + delta u'. The next page turns to inequalities among the semi-axes a, b, c. These include a < c < b - 2a, b > 2a + c, 8a^2 - 4ab - 3b^2 > 0, and c^2 = a^2(4a^2 - b^2)/(b^2 - a^2) as the boundary alpha = 0. It finds the critical ratio from 2a^2 = b^2 - 2ab, i.e. b = (1+sqrt3)a, together with c < (2 - sqrt3)b and b^2 - a^2 > (2sqrt3+3)a^2.

This page (right column, top). A struck-out line, then something like e_1 = ... (e_2 - e_1)/(...). Next comes a power-type expression (e_2 - e e_1)^(...). Then a chain of inequalities:
- p - e_1 > (... + 3)^... ;
- < (2...)^... ;
- p > (... + 1)^... ;
- ... < (...)^... .

My inference: these are the same critical-ratio conditions as on 2v, written in auxiliary variables (e_1, e_2 possibly squared axes or their ratios, p a squared ratio). Plausible matches are p - e_1 > (2sqrt3 + 3)e_1, the analogue of b^2 - a^2 > (2sqrt3+3)a^2, and p > (sqrt3 + 1)^2 e_1, the analogue of b > (1+sqrt3)a. This is not verifiable from the image.

This page (right margin). Further bounds s > ..., s < ..., ... > ... + ..., and s > ... < (... - 1)... appear. These are plausibly bounds of the type a < c < b - 2a, i.e. an admissible interval for one axis.

This page (centre). There is a long fraction with a horizontal bar, then bounds rho > (... - ...)/(...(... - ...)) and rho < .../.... These are presumably bounds for a ratio of the form a^2(b^2 - 4a^2)/(b^2 - a^2) seen on 2v.

This page (left). A formula ... = .../sqrt(...(... - ...)) appears, possibly a frequency or root of a characteristic equation. There is also a small crossed diagram suggesting a sign case-split, and expressions (... - e_1) - ... and a > ... + c (cf. b > 2a + c on 2v).

Overall purpose (inferred). Riemann is determining, for the perturbation problem of the preceding page, the region of axis ratios in which a certain discriminant or coefficient has a given sign, i.e. a stability or realness condition. He is locating its boundary at the ratio 1 + sqrt3.
errors: No step can be checked reliably because the formulas are essentially illegible.
Related constants on the following page are mutually consistent: (1+sqrt3)^2 = 4 + 2sqrt3, so (b/a)^2 - 1 = 3 + 2sqrt3, and 1/(2+sqrt3) = 2 - sqrt3.
There is one probable slip on the next page, not this one: the step 'c < (sqrt3+1)/(sqrt3+2)' omits the factor b and seems to be an intermediate scribble.

results.what: Tentative: inequality conditions on axis ratios of a fluid ellipsoid (with a critical ratio involving 1 + sqrt3 and 2sqrt3 + 3) bounding the region where the linearized perturbation problem has a given character
results.modern_name: Stability/existence domain of Riemann ellipsoids (linear stability analysis)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1861 (published paper on fluid ellipsoids); the stability analysis was later corrected and completed by Lebovitz and Chandrasekhar (1960s), 'Ellipsoidal Figures of Equilibrium' 1969

deep.surprise_reason: These are scratch computations of inequalities among axis ratios, belonging to Riemann's known and published work on rotating fluid ellipsoids. Nothing legible goes beyond routine working toward results in the 1861 paper.

transcription_corrections: The machine transcription's '[?]' readings are mostly unverifiable. The image shows mainly faded or bleed-through ink in three clusters: the right column top, a centre fraction band, and the left lower region.

The left half of the page also carries legible-looking but extremely faint fragments not in the transcription: a crossed diagram with inequalities, 'a > ... + c', a radical expression '.../sqrt(...(...-...))', and several short lines near the bottom-left.
The right-column inequalities likely contain the constants 2sqrt3+3 and sqrt3+1 (cf. next page), so '(...+3)' is probably '(2sqrt3+3)' and '(...+1)' probably '(sqrt3+1)'. This is tentative.
